sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for timeline page
sections.what: Loads icons, buttons, the event card parts, the server connection, the auth store and the page navigation helper.
sections.why: These are needed to draw the timeline, fetch its events and move between pages.

sections.name: mapBackendTypeToFrontend
sections.title: Event type mapping
sections.what: Converts each server event type into one of the card types. Lab results, vitals and AI insights become reports. Prescriptions and medication changes become medication cards. Symptoms and diagnoses become diagnosis cards. Visits, hospital stays and vaccinations become visit cards. Surgery has its own type. Anything else becomes a reminder.
sections.why: The interface draws only a few card styles, so the server's longer list of types has to be squeezed into them.
sections.watch_out: The fallback sends any unknown or new event type to the reminder style, so new kinds of health events will look like reminders until this list is updated.

sections.name: getSubtitle
sections.title: Event subtitle builder
sections.what: Builds the small line under an event title. It reads the stored details and uses the first useful value it finds, such as provider name, doctor name, lab name or dosage. If none exist, it uses the reference type or a default label.
sections.why: Gives each card a useful second line without asking the server for a separate text field.
sections.watch_out: The code reads the details as text or as an object, so the expected format must match what the server stores. A parsing error is ignored silently.

sections.name: formatSeverity
sections.title: Severity text formatter
sections.what: Turns a severity word from all capitals into a capitalised first letter with the rest in lowercase, for example turning a stored word into a friendlier display. Empty values show as nothing.
sections.why: Makes severity read more naturally on the card.
sections.watch_out: It only changes the case of the text. It does not translate or check that the severity is one of the expected values.

sections.name: HealthTimelinePage (part 1)
sections.title: Loading and converting timeline events
sections.what: When the page opens, asks the backend for up to 100 health events for the selected profile. Each event is converted into the simpler shape the screen uses, including a readable date and an attached document link if one exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: the backend returns raw records, and the screen needs friendlier fields. Reason for the exact date format is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Errors are only written to the browser console, so a failed load looks like an empty page with no message to the user.

sections.name: HealthTimelinePage: if
sections.title: Reloading on profile change and pin toggling
sections.what: Loads the timeline again when a different profile is selected. Pinning or unpinning an event updates the screen at once, then saves the change; if saving fails, the whole list is reloaded to undo the visual change.
sections.why: The instant update makes the screen feel quick. The reload on failure puts the screen back in line with what is saved.
sections.watch_out: The screen can show a pin as set until the reload finishes, and the failure path only logs to the console with no message to the user.

sections.name: HealthTimelinePage: if
sections.title: Year grouping, summary counts and header
sections.what: Groups the visible events by year, newest year first. Counts reports and visits for the sidebar and shows a 'Patient Since' date taken from the last event in the list. The header shows the page title and buttons.
sections.why: Grouping by year gives the long history a simple structure. Reason for taking the last event as the oldest is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: 'Patient Since' assumes the last event is the oldest, which is only true if the backend sends newest first. The code does not check this.

sections.name: HealthTimelinePage (part 4)
sections.title: Search, filter tabs and sidebar
sections.what: Provides a search box that matches event text and filter buttons for All, Report, Medication and Visit. The sidebar shows the Patient Since date and counts.
sections.why: Lets the user narrow a long history quickly. Reason the filters are applied in the screen rather than the backend is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The filter buttons are shown but the filtering only changes how the list is grouped in the screen, so a count can differ from what the user sees if events are missing from the loaded 100.

sections.name: HealthTimelinePage (part 5)
sections.title: Share card, timeline list and empty state
sections.what: Shows a 'Share Records' card with a Manage Access button that does nothing yet. Below it, shows a loading message, the grouped event cards, or a 'no records found' message when nothing matches.
sections.why: Shows the list state the user is in. The share button has no action in the code, which suggests the feature is not finished.
sections.watch_out: Manage Access has no click handler, so users may think sharing works when it does not.

summary: The health timeline page that turns server events into readable cards, including labels, subtitles and a severity display.
purpose: Lets the user review their health history in order, with each event shown in plain terms.
why: The server stores several kinds of events, and this page translates them into the small set of card types the interface draws.
how: The page maps each server event type to a card type, such as report, medication, diagnosis, visit or surgery. It builds a short subtitle from the stored details when they exist. It also turns a severity word into a readable form. The rest of the file, not shown here, loads the events and draws the cards.
inputs: Event records from the server, each with a type, optional details in text or object form, and a reference type.
outputs: Card type labels, subtitle text and readable severity text for the timeline cards.
risks: Unknown event types fall back to the reminder card type, which can mislabel a new kind of event. Subtitle text is taken from stored details, so unexpected details could show odd text.
debug: If an event shows the wrong icon or card type, check the switch that maps event types. If a subtitle is wrong, check the detail fields it tries in order. If the severity looks off, check the value sent by the server.
